# Mass and centre of gravity

> *Infrastructure test chapter: its text is a placeholder until the pilot translation. It exercises every construction the deliverables have to handle.*

## The datum and the arm

The **datum** is the reference line from which every arm is measured. A mass of 80 kg with an arm of −0.45 m gives a moment of −36 kg·m.

@fig-07-cap01-envolvente-centrado shows the four cases worked out in this chapter, and @tbl-07-cap01-hoja-centrado a loading sheet.

![The four loading cases against the permitted CG range.](imagenes/07-cap01-envolvente-centrado.png){#fig-07-cap01-envolvente-centrado fig-alt="Mass against CG position, with the permitted range shaded."}

| Item | Mass (kg) | Arm (m) | Moment (kg·m) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Glider | 300 | 0.60 | 180 |
| Pilot | 80 | −0.45 | −36 |
| **Total** | **380** | **0.38** | **144** |
: Example loading sheet for a single-seater {#tbl-07-cap01-hoja-centrado}

::: {.callout-warning title="Safety"}
An aft CG can make a spin unrecoverable.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Regulation"}
The flight manual limits are mandatory.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Golden rule"}
Weigh yourself with your parachute on.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Airmanship"}
Check the ballast before every flight, not only the first one of the day.
:::

::: {.ejercicio}
**Exercise 1 — Fin ballast.**

Where is the CG with 5 L of fin ballast?

**Solution.** It moves aft to +0.373 m.
:::
